shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on approach to an airport, in daylight and visual conditions.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring.

What happened. Late in the arrival, a bird strike occurred on the runway the crew had set up for, and the approach was changed to an instrument landing system approach to a different runway. The captain entered the new approach and the crew continued. Air traffic control vectored the aircraft to intercept the final approach course and cleared it for the approach. During the intercept, with the navigation mode armed and the altitude selector set to the final approach fix altitude of 1,600 ft, the aircraft was descending, and the first officer was using the speed brakes to slow to an assigned 180 knots. The first officer had not yet called for flaps. Air traffic control then vectored the aircraft off the approach. The first officer entered the assigned heading and did not retract the speed brakes. The aircraft descended below its assigned altitude and kept descending as the speed approached the low-speed limit. The captain noticed and began to correct, but the aircraft descended to 2,100 ft and the stick shaker activated. The captain took control, called for flaps 1, and climbed back to 2,500 ft, with the speed back in the normal range at the assigned 180 knots.
safe_outcome: The captain then handed control back to the first officer, who landed the aircraft without further incident. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was descending nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.
bracket_fill: [climbing / descending / crossing] = descending; [this aircraft] = this aircraft
notes: Single narrative (first officer, pilot flying). Rule 3, removed: the 'Cause' section (quick ATC instructions, 'aggressive' descent profile, runway change, late flap call) and the 'Suggestions' section (what the first officer should have done with flaps and speed brakes). 'Did not call for flaps soon enough' replaced by the observable 'had not yet called for flaps'; 'but it was too late' dropped. Rule 5, moved to the safe ending: control handed back and the landing. Rule 6: both runway identifiers removed. Judgement calls: the report says the captain 'retracted flaps', but also that flaps had not been called for and the speed brakes were still out, so the item retracted is unclear; written as 'began to correct'. 'Red line approached' read as the low-speed limit, given the stick shaker followed. The bird strike is kept as ambiguous as the report ('occurred on the runway'); whether it involved this aircraft is not stated. Bracket 'descending': the aircraft went below its assigned altitude after being taken off the approach, then climbed; other approach traffic would be descending nearby.
